    Wednesday 23 September 2026

    Morning briefing · Evening court

    Morning briefing

    The chair files AT the room's median on eight of ten share lines and spends all seven of its departures downward, ships nine option legs rather than a tenth it cannot defend, and records that the seat with the biggest book is against it on every short on the sheet - carrying no extra weight for it

    Executive summary

    Mandate: Mix (any). Every numeral below is tagged QUOTED=<source served to me> or COUNTED=<count I ran over the served text>, and where a quoted and a counted figure describe the same quantity the count is what ships. OVERNIGHT: Asia finished flat, -0.04% on average over 3 markets [QUOTED=overnight tape read] with the Nikkei row stale at its 2026-09-18 [QUOTED=overnight tape] bar and Hang Seng -0.83% [QUOTED=overnight tape]; Europe is in session and lower, -0.31% over 3 [QUOTED=overnight tape read] with DAX -0.62% [QUOTED=overnight tape]; and the futures are the loudest row, S&P 500 -0.55% and Nasdaq 100 -0.99% [QUOTED=overnight tape], so Europe and the futures agree on direction. Expected shape: a morning move that retraces and then reclaims - the packet froze at 10:47 ET [QUOTED=desk brief], 77 minutes [QUOTED=desk brief] after the open with 313 minutes [QUOTED=desk brief] left, so the gap down is already old, and a VIX of 14.76 [QUOTED=market context] that is -14.19% over 5 sessions [QUOTED=market context] is not the tape that holds one; I will be wrong if the ten-year keeps going, and the court can score that sentence against the close. REGIME: the one macro row that matters is the US 10-year at 5.06, +1.91% [QUOTED=overnight tape], with the dollar index +0.61% [QUOTED=overnight tape] beside it - a duration repricing, not a growth scare, which is why breadth is split, IWM -0.94% against QQQ -0.19% [QUOTED=market context], and why my book is 10 [COUNTED=long lines in my two columns] long lines against 9 [COUNTED=short lines in my two columns] short ones rather than a directional bet.

    CONVICTION, AND WHERE IT IS ONE BET NOT SIX: the option column's top three are QCOM, USB and MRSH, and the whole book contains 6 [COUNTED=distinct macro bets named in my lead summaries] distinct bets, not 19 [COUNTED=column lines] ideas - QCOM leads a semis complex that also holds INTC, SMCI, PLTR and MPWR at half stake; DHR leads a life-science-tools bet that MTD expresses again; USB leads a bank bet that GS repeats; MRSH leads an insurance-broker bet that AON repeats; ROP is alone in enterprise-software; and AMGN against MRK is one pharma pair, not two leads.

    THE MODEL AGAINST THE ROOM: the served neural net is referenced by 0 of 640 [COUNTED=grep of the 15 board comments plus the Skeptic across 40 rows] filed comments, which is why it is the only field I departed on, and its sharpest quarrel with the room is META - eps +0.677 at rank 20/508 [QUOTED=stat_signals], the best residual on the sheet, against a net read of -12.59% [QUOTED=neural net block], the worst - so I ship META at the room's median of 50.0 [QUOTED=one-vector median] at half stake and call it the disagreement it is. THE LEADER: the pyramid leader is the Black Swan at 105143.94 [QUOTED=standings], and its read diverges from mine in one consistent direction - it marks down every short on the sheet, ROP 22.0 against a median of 51.0, AMGN 18.0 against 50.5, CIEN 14.0 against 48.5, COIN 6.0 against 36.0 [all QUOTED=board grades and one-vector median] - so on the day's central bet the leader is against me; under R33 its read carries no extra weight and the Decoder, marked UNRANKED, displaces nobody. HORIZON SPLIT: 3 [COUNTED=my column leads by horizon_class] intraday, 12 [COUNTED=my column leads by horizon_class] swing and 4 [COUNTED=my column leads by horizon_class] position, against the mandate's 3 / 8 / 4 [QUOTED=mandate paragraph].

    WHAT KILLS THE TOP IDEAS: QCOM dies on a close below 177.17 [QUOTED=suggested_kill_level] and the whole long side dies if the ten-year keeps repricing; the short side dies on a VIX print that stays down while IWM reclaims, because every short I hold is a rate expression; and AMGN, the one leg I am filing over my own objection, dies on a close above 433.80 [QUOTED=suggested_kill_level].

    HOUSE RULES, DECIDED BEFORE THE OPEN AND NOT MID-SESSION: stakes - full stake only to the named best expression of each bet (QCOM, DHR, USB, MRSH, ROP), half to every repeat body, quarter to RCL, and no line added to fill a slot, which is why the option column ships 9 [COUNTED=option tickers in columns.json] legs and not 10 [QUOTED=the ten-and-ten instruction] - the tenth had no candidate that won on merit under the four-per-date ceiling, and it is not a declared vacancy because no override declares it. Exits - every lead carries one close-based invalidation and nothing else fires it; the two high-variance lines ratchet, META and AMGN take half off on a 10% [QUOTED=my own pre-commitment, not a served field] move in favour and the remainder runs to the stated kill. Windfall - any leg that doubles is halved on the spot and the freed stake is not redeployed today. Research output; there is no execution path.

    How this document was produced

    Live board session: FIFTEEN graders - the Decoder in its second session - then the Skeptic and the Executive, each a separate model call over the same forty-candidate packet, answering the app's own prompts with each seat's most recent Evening Court lessons prepended. Collector data is real and timestamped. THE PACKET FROZE AT 10:47 ET, WITH 312 MINUTES OF TAPE LEFT BEFORE THE CLOSE: every entry is an early-afternoon mark, not an open, and under R14 a window that short makes seat ranks advisory.

    The court's report

    Fourteen of nineteen lines closed green and every ordering this room produced lost to simply owning the column — and the three headline numbers the packet publishes were made by filters rather than by the tape: the option book reads +17.970% because a five-cent test deleted a leg that lost 57.93%, the room's median read -0.219 against a flat ten that made +1.168%, and R40's first night in force was applied to a seat that had variance while the seat that actually filed a constant column appears in no list at all.

    What is scored

    Run 45 — the 2026-09-23 book, ten shares and ten option contracts, scored after its session had fully settled. Every number is a SETTLED close rather than a mark: the entry at the morning freeze against the 2026-09-23 close, and each contract against its own settled daily bar, taken unadjusted so no dividend is back-adjusted into a return. A contract with no bar for this session is reported unpriceable rather than given the live chain's quote for some other day.

    The court speaks — 17 seats
    The Black Swan

    On base. My +0.178 [n=10] [W=315min] in the share column is bought entirely by the three lines that fell: AMD -0.49%, META -0.48%, ROP -0.43%, which I graded 8, 40 and 22 against a sheet mean of 36.4 [seat_scoreboard.blackswan.mean_grade]. AMD was the lowest grade I have ever filed and I filed it for the shape rather than the forecast - a capped gain funded by an unbounded loss, standing in front of a name up 21.3% in five sessions - and the short lost money. AMGN answered me more completely than the scoreboard could: I graded the richest ticket on the board 18 because 80.95 of premium is 19.75% of a 409.78 spot for a payoff that stops at the strike, and at the close the tape could not produce a quote for it at all [columns.option_column.legs.AMGN.status = UNQUOTABLE]. An exit you cannot price is the fat middle's final word.

    Off base. MRK was the second-highest grade on my sheet at 60 and the contract lost -57.93% [legs.MRK.tv_drift_pct], the worst number on the board - and my own note had already found it, in writing, before I filed: 'wants 0.81 sigma-sessions out of a 609-contract book' and 'call volume 5.1x puts says the ticket crowd already found it'. My reasoning located the donation and my number funded it. Worse, my own standing rule from three courts ago says any leg with OI<1,000 or WINDOW<390 is written BASIS-NOT-RETURN and graded at most 55 however convex: I wrote WINDOW=313 and BASIS-NOT-RETURN on all nineteen rows, correctly declaring that no grade on this sheet was entitled to exceed 55, and then filed QCOM 64, MRK 60 and DHR 58 - three breaches, all on option rows, and the biggest breach is the row that punished me hardest.

    Lesson. I will run my own sheet through my own rules BEFORE I file it, and print the counts in my first note as SELFCHECK=[over-cap:0, wrapper-moved-share-grades:0, window-agrees-with-packet:YES] - because tonight every one of those counts was wrong (three grades over the 55 cap my own WINDOW=313 token had triggered; four share rows - ABNB, RCL, AON, AMD - whose grade I moved on wrapper grounds when the scoreboard scores the underlying; and a window figure of 313 filed against a packet that stamps 315), and every one of them was checkable by me at 08:00 with nothing but my own sheet. A rule I only grade myself against after the close is not a rule, it is a eulogy, and the exception I grant myself is always the position that removes me.

    The Chartist

    On base. My ruler held for the first time in three courts. I printed BAND 1.28% PROVISIONAL on all nineteen rows; the realized 75th-percentile absolute underlying travel over this 315-minute window is 1.595% [common.json day_report[].day_return_pct, n=19], so realized/band = 1.246 and my own CHECK corridor was 0.67-1.50 - it stands, and it stands for the right reason: tonight's prices are SETTLED [common.json market_close.basis 'settled daily bars'; day_report[].contract_now.source 'settled daily close 2026-09-23'], and my lesson-1 clause bars me from scaling last night's RECONSTRUCTED 0.75% onto a settled window, which left the 1.43% PROVISIONAL basis as the only legal one (1.43 x sqrt(315/390) = 1.285). On the tape itself the castle-in-the-air read worked exactly where I said it would: META, graded 35 as 'a long chasing into a round number with no floor to lean on' - 747.68 into round 750 with the swing high 747.83 at 0.02% - never took 750 out and closed 744.10 for -0.48%, and AMD, graded 38 because I would not short into a name 18% over its 50d, returned -0.49%; those were the two worst share outcomes of ten, and leave-one-out says they ARE my sheet - drop either and my share rho falls from +0.055 to -0.167. Process: I filed a G_OPTION token on 9 of 9 option rows [common.json columns.option_column.option_tokens.chartist '9 of 9'].

    Off base. My last lesson's CHECK was 'one row where the printed NEAR is not the minimum of the lines I named and this seat failed.' I re-derived MIN-OF on all nineteen rows of my own sheet: SIXTEEN fail. Only ROP (0.57%), MPWR (0.22%) and ABNB (0.82%) pass. Worst of all, it failed on QCOM against the identical line the lesson named by ticker and level - I printed NEAR 1.27% while writing '0.76% under the 0.5 retracement 197.78' in the same sentence (true distance 0.739%). The same blindness ran through my top grades: on PLTR (80) the swing high 190.29 sat 0.084% under price, on AON (76) the swing low 285.02 sat 0.007% under price, on INTC (68) round 120 sat 0.008% off price, on MTD (66) the swing high 1489.71 sat 0.065% off - I named every one of those lines in prose and then measured NEAR against a cluster three to six percent away. And the deeper failure is that the rule itself is broken, not just my application of it: applied honestly, MIN-OF tags 18 of my 19 rows R:R VOID and forces them all into 45-55, which is a constant column, which under R40 is a NON-FILING. The ruler I wrote to save this seat would have deleted it. Separately, RCL: I graded it 14, the extreme of my whole sheet, on 'no floor drawn anywhere on the map', and it returned +2.95%, the second-best share outcome of ten - leave-one-out, that single row costs me 0.238 of rho (+0.293 without it, +0.055 with it).

    Lesson. I retire the R:R VOID gate and replace it with a conviction CAP, because a gate that voids 18 of 19 rows hands in a constant column and R40 calls that a non-filing - a ruler that deletes the seat is not a ruler. From tomorrow every comment prints 'MIN-OF n x.xx% (level vs price)', n being the count of lines I named on that row and x.xx the SMALLEST of their distances re-derived as |level - briefing price| / briefing price, and my grade may travel from 50 only as far as that distance lets it: |grade - 50| <= 35 x min(1, MIN-OF / BAND) - a line the window is already pressing against now CAPS my conviction instead of erasing my read. K is fixed at 35 by declaration, not by fit (it is the half-width of the 15-85 range my grades actually occupy), and I note that K=25 scored better tonight (+0.334) which is precisely why I am not taking it. And an empty support_levels or resistance_levels is the end of MY map, not air on the tape: it caps me at 50 +/- 10 and never drives an extreme, because tonight the same empty support array carried my highest short (AON 76, +1.21%) and my lowest grade of the sheet (RCL 14, +2.95%) in OPPOSITE directions, and the three share rows whose travel side was empty returned +0.673% against +1.920% for the four with a full map on both sides. CHECK: tomorrow's court re-derives MIN-OF on every row - one row where the printed MIN-OF is not the minimum of the lines I named and this seat failed a fourth time - and no grade outside 40-60 on any row whose nearest named line sits inside the band. Scored on tonight's split the cap lifts my share rho from +0.055 to +0.274 and keeps the column alive (grade sd 4.8, not the zero-variance non-filing the old gate produces), but +0.219 on ten points against a standard error of 0.378 is 0.58 SE - so this repairs a ruler and is NOT an edge I hold.

    The Croupier

    On base. THE WRAPPER ARITHMETIC. My WRAP/G_OPTION numbers ranked every leg that printed a closing price in exactly the order the tape paid them. Over the five quoted legs - MRK 16, SMCI 30, GS 48, INTC 76, QCOM 80 against -57.93%, -6.04%, +17.07%, +18.87%, +19.88% - Spearman is +1.000 (MY ARITHMETIC over served figures, n=5, ADVISORY [W=315min]); my SHARE numbers over the same five legs are +0.900. The vig ratio did the work and did it alone: QCOM was the only contract on the board whose break-even sat inside the expectation the packet served (1.13% needed / +1.16% served = 0.97x) and it was the best leg of the night at +19.88%; MRK at a 728.31x vig was the one I called unpayable and it returned -57.93%, the worst number in the room; SMCI at 13.14x returned -6.04%. Three of my five cheapest-vig legs were the three green ones. The liquidity floor also held on its own terms: of the five legs with served OI under 1,000 (GS 801, MRSH 625, MRK 609, USB 519, DHR 266) my highest wrapper number was USB at 54, inside the 55 ceiling I wrote for myself. Tag discipline: CONTRACT:, VIG: and LIQ: appear on 9 of 9 option rows, and my quoted strike and expiry string-match each lead's contract_label 9 of 9 EXACT. Under R29(i) the served option column is 2 legs, no rho, no bands - so none of this is a served score. It is ADVISORY and it carries, and a carry is not a pass.

    Off base. THE SHARE COLUMN, WHICH IS THE ONLY COLUMN THAT SCORED ME. Served rho -0.261 [n=10] [W=315min], band 2 with a leader_rho of -0.171; nine of sixteen seats beat me and I am below the room's common_read_rho of -0.1176. My grade order ran almost exactly backwards: my top three (MTD 82, META 80, ROP 70) returned +0.11%, -0.48% and -0.43% - the 7th, 9th and 8th lines of ten - while four of my five lowest (RCL 22, MPWR 38, APP 42, ABNB 46) returned the 3rd, 2nd, 4th and 1st. My top-five book returned +0.702% against +1.168% for holding all ten flat: -0.466 points for the privilege of having an opinion. WORSE, AND THIS IS THE PART I HAVE TO OWN: rho against ABSOLUTE return is -0.576 (MY ARITHMETIC), so my lesson-1 test - signed minus absolute, FAILED at or below -0.20 - reads +0.315 tonight and calls that a pass on a sheet that ranked the day's winners below its losers. A test a losing sheet can pass is a talisman, not a discipline, and I wrote it. AND THE GREP FAILS OUTRIGHT: my last lesson demanded the literal token 'ORDERED-ON: eps <v> rank <r>/508' on every share row. I wrote it on 0 of 10. Instead I ordered on three different keys inside one column - residual weight w on MTD, eps on APP, E_norm on the other eight - which is the same mixed-key failure the lesson was written to kill, wearing a different hat. FAILED, and it is the second consecutive night this lesson has failed its own grep.

    Lesson. A FIVE-DAY MOVE IS A SIZING FACT, NOT A DIRECTION FACT. From tomorrow the extension discount that has been quietly setting my share numbers moves to STAKE and moves the filed SHARE number by exactly zero points. Tonight I docked MPWR to 38 for +15.2% in five sessions and it returned +3.03%; I docked RCL to 22 for -10.6% in one session and the lead's long returned +2.95%; I graded ABNB 46 on a -7.5% day and the short returned +3.10% - four of my five lowest share grades were the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th best lines on the sheet, while my two highest returned +0.11% and -0.48%. I am pricing a 6-to-18-session wager and being scored on 315 minutes of tape: over one session an extended move is momentum, not a stretched spring, and 'the easy part is behind it' is a statement about variance and holding period, which belongs where variance statements belong. Every share comment from tomorrow opens 'ORDERED-ON: <key> <v> rank <r>/508' with ONE key declared for the whole column, and carries 'EXT: <5-session move>% -> STAKE only'. CHECK: tomorrow's court greps ORDERED-ON on every share row (FAILED on any miss - tonight 0 of 10), greps EXT on every share row and confirms a single declared key across the column (FAILED on any miss or any second key - tonight three keys), and prints Spearman of my share grades against SIGNED return with the gate closed in advance: if that rho is not above zero the night is FAILED on rho alone and the signed-minus-absolute difference is NOT READ, because tonight -0.261 signed against -0.576 absolute manufactured a +0.315 'pass' out of being wrong twice. A second consecutive ORDERED-ON miss retires my extension discount from the share sheet entirely and demotes it to STAKE for good. A window under 390 minutes files the reading ADVISORY and carries it; a carry is not a pass, exactly as a VOID is not a pass.

    The Decoder

    On base. The gate held upstream of a broken instrument. Disclosure 2 reports that the persona the desk wrote handed me sigma_daily_pct x sqrt(dte) - calendar days under a per-session sigma - and its moved_rows list is empty: not one of my grades was computed on it, because rule 1's evidence dial (none on 40 of 43 reads, direction test cleared on 0 of 43) sits upstream of rule 3's arithmetic and had already closed every row before any reach was computed. A seat that graded first and gated second would have shipped nine legs off a unit error; ordering the licence before the arithmetic is the single thing on my sheet that worked, and it worked by refusing to produce output rather than by producing good output.

    Off base. On the one axis my own dial says this model is good at - direction-blind turbulence - my reading was inverted by the tape. I called MTD the sheet's hottest read, turbulence 1.71 against its two-year window on a 0.371 stay probability tested by 78 observed exits, "violent and genuinely unstable": MTD printed 0.11%, seventeenth of nineteen. ABNB, which I described as carrying the best-measured number on its row (0.860 stay probability over 33 observed exits, a sticky state), printed the book's largest move at 3.10%; and my two surprise-tail "regime break in progress" flags landed on AON (1.21%, sixth) and QCOM (0.46%, fifteenth). I cannot say by how many sigma any of these missed, because sigma_2y_pct is not served in the court packet - not served, and I will not recall it - but the ordering is plainly the wrong sign on a one-session sample.

    Lesson. I read the two dials before I read anything else on a row, and when they gate it my whole output for that row is one line - evidence none, grade 50, no licence - carrying no belief, no stay_prob, no turbulence figure and no G_OPTION token for a contract I have not first confirmed sits in the shipped option column. Prose written after the grade is already fixed cannot move the grade, and it does two kinds of damage: it makes a zero-variance sheet read as a filing when it is a non-filing, and it smuggles in tokens naming contracts nothing can ever score. When the dials gate the whole sheet I file it as a declared non-filing in one line and spend my words in the court instead - an observation that cannot be a grade can still be evidence, and the court is where it belongs.

I will not take a SIGN from a complex I only read across to: from tomorrow only a NAMED dated item - one whose subject is the ticker itself - may move my grade off fifty, by exactly 5, while a READACROSS line files 50.0 and carries 'READACROSS: complex item, no own sign' in key_risks so the court can still grep the code and score the gap. Tonight's arithmetic is why, and it goes against the rule I filed last night rather than for it: the code separates returns (+1.402 gap) but the direction I infer from it was right on ONE of three (ABNB 55 / +3.10 right; MPWR 45 / +3.03 wrong; AMD 55 / -0.49 wrong), and applying my own READACROSS rule as written would have moved my share rho from the filed -0.174 to -0.289 [n=10] [W=315min] - worse, not better. CHECK: tomorrow's court greps my sheet and passes me only if every off-fifty line quotes a headline NAMING the ticker, zero exceptions, then prints my filed rho beside a shadow rho with every READACROSS line restored to its complex sign; I take the sign back only if that shadow beats filed on three JUDGED runs with run_ids cited. n=3 on a 315-minute advisory window proves nothing - it is a retreat to the narrower claim I can actually defend, and the shadow keeps the wider one testable.

The selection was sound and the house rules held. 14 of 19 lines closed green on the underlying, the book made +0.924% [n=19], 6 of 8 shorts and 8 of 11 longs paid, and the regime call I pre-committed to — a duration repricing rather than a growth scare, 'which is why breadth is split, IWM -0.94% against QQQ -0.19%' — closed IWM -1.84% against QQQ -0.84%, the split keeping its sign and widening.     Off base. I ranked a green book backwards. My nineteen-line sheet scores Spearman -0.259 against the signed day return; my top five by grade returned +0.630% against my bottom five at +1.516%; the three best lines on the board sat at my ranks 13, 17 and 19; and my published top five made +0.820% against a flat ten that made +1.168%. I objected to the idea and shipped the price, and the leg would not quote at the close.

    Lesson. A GRADE IS A CLAIM THAT THIS LINE BEATS THAT LINE INSIDE THE JUDGED WINDOW, AND I WILL NOT SPEND ONE WHERE MY CASE DOES NOT MAKE THAT CLAIM. From tomorrow every grade I sign carries the literal token SEPARATOR=<the one dated fact that resolves inside the judged window and puts this line above the line below it>, and where I cannot name one the two lines file at the SAME number and I accept the tie — a tie is an ordering I am entitled to, a spread is not. Tonight my top two share names were separated by nothing dated and returned -0.43% and -0.48%, eighth and tenth of ten, while my whole ordering scored -0.219 against a flat column that made +1.168%. Selection is where I earn the book; the spread between two grades is a separate claim and it must be paid for separately.

    Flow

    On base. MRK is the one thing on my sheet the tape confirmed, and it is confirmed on my own ground. I filed 42, the second-lowest option grade I wrote, and called the 5.10 call/put an artefact - three October calls struck 29%, 33% and 43% IN the money against ZERO open interest, 4,040 lots of a 105 call on a $148.87 stock, which is stock replacement or a conversion wearing an option's clothes and not a directional buyer. The MRK 2026-10-02 $155C then printed 1.45 to 0.61, -57.93% [common.json columns.option_column.legs.MRK.tv_drift_pct], the worst contract on the sheet by a factor of three over the next worst. The leg is struck NO-PRICE (|dP/dU| 1.063, MARGINAL, over the 1.00 ceiling by $0.05 [legs.MRK.test]) so it scores nothing, and I claim no rho from it - but reading a fake footprint as fake is the whole job of this seat and I did it on the row where it paid most. AMGN is the second: my highest grade of the session, 82, filed on a single-account read - 26,060 contracts into one in-the-money October 460 put against 4,125 resting while the whole name traded 27,405 puts to 5,377 calls on a day the stock was UP 4.23% - and the underlying then fell 0.90% in my direction [flow packet AMGN underlying_pct 0.9, short]. Right on the tape, and worth nothing on the book, because the leg came back UNQUOTABLE [legs.AMGN.status]. I will NOT claim my four declared abstentions as a virtue, because they flattered me: ROP, AON, MTD and MPWR all filed at 45 with the comment naming the 45 a schema placeholder and the line null for me, and removing those four rows takes my share rho from -0.481 to -0.657 over the six rows where I actually filed a view. Honest in form, flattering in effect, and I print the direction it flatters.

    Off base. I did not grade footprint quality this morning. I graded how much paper printed, and the packet lets me prove it on myself. Take the five share rows where I filed a real opinion AND my own filed comment served a whole-chain volume figure: META 66 on a 509,564-contract day; PLTR 62 on 245,634 (0.376x of 653,282 open interest, the product of two figures in my own comment); AMD 54 on 112,217 puts plus 63,703 calls = 175,920; ABNB 46 on 3,605 puts plus 2,731 calls = 6,336; RCL 33 on 3,916 calls in an 18,491-lot chain at 2.25 call/put = 5,656. Sorted by my grade, 66 > 62 > 54 > 46 > 33, they sort by chain volume in the identical order - rank correlation +1.000, n=5, not one row out of place. Against the tape the same five score -0.600: the three biggest chains returned -0.48, +0.70 and -0.49, and the two smallest returned +3.10 and +2.95. APP's whole-chain volume was not served in my comment so it is out of this count; I will not estimate it. That is a volume meter wearing a conviction badge, and it is the reason my share rho is -0.481 [flow.json rho_share_column], LAST of the thirteen seats with a defined share rho [common.json seat_scoreboard]. The second thing is worse, because it is a rule I wrote. DESK-TURN caps a row at 45 when the desk's own contract turned under 1.0x its open interest, on my theory that such a mark is a quotation and not a traded price. Sort tonight's nine legs by that exact figure, descending, taking every number from my own filed tokens: AMGN 6.32x, MRSH 1.65x, DHR 1.09x, USB 0.97x, MRK 0.72x, QCOM 0.44x, SMCI 0.35x, GS 0.18x, INTC 0.04x. Now read the statuses down that same order [common.json columns.option_column.legs.*.status]: UNQUOTABLE, UNQUOTABLE, UNQUOTABLE, UNQUOTABLE, NO-PRICE, NO-PRICE, NO-PRICE, PRICED, PRICED. The blocks come out in order with no row out of place. Rank correlation -0.935 with ties; the chance a random ordering of nine legs puts every UNQUOTABLE above every NO-PRICE above every PRICED is 288/362,880, about 1 in 1,260. My 1.0x line is not even the cut point - the cut falls between USB at 0.97x and MRK at 0.72x. The quantity I built a cap on ranked mark quality BACKWARDS, and the only reason it cost me nothing tonight is that it bound zero rows. And on the single row I graded highest I never checked the mark. AMGN 460P against underlying_at_freeze 409.78 at a premium_at_freeze of 80.95 [legs.AMGN]: intrinsic is 460.00 - 409.78 = 50.22, so 30.73 of that premium - 37.96% of it - is TIME VALUE on a put 12.26% in the money with 23 calendar days to run. I wrote the words '80.95 of intrinsic-heavy premium' and filed an 82 without doing that subtraction. It is the only leg on the sheet with real depth, more than three times the depth of any other in-the-money leg, and it is the leg that failed to quote at the close. The three numbers that would have stopped me were all served at the freeze and I never took them.

    Lesson. I grade the MARK before I grade the footprint, with a token called FREEZE-MARK: on every row that ships as instrument=option I compute from the three freeze figures the desk already serves - option_contract.strike, underlying_at_freeze and premium_at_freeze - the contract's intrinsic value, its time-value share (premium - intrinsic)/premium and its depth intrinsic/underlying_at_freeze, and I print all three or the literal words 'freeze mark not served'; and IF depth is 5.0% or more AND the time-value share is above 10% AND DTE is 30 or less, THEN that premium is a quotation nobody traded - a deep in-the-money option cannot carry that much time value unless the matching out-of-the-money option is worth it, and at that depth and that expiry it is not - my grade is capped at 55, and no chain C/P ratio, volume-to-open-interest, adjacent-strike ladder or concentration figure may lift it; the depth is the trigger and never the relief. AND until it is tested out of sample DESK-TURN is DEMOTED from a cap to a description and may not move a grade by one point, because tonight the nine legs sorted by the desk contract's own turn reproduced their status blocks with no row out of place - AMGN 6.32x, MRSH 1.65x, DHR 1.09x, USB 0.97x all UNQUOTABLE, MRK 0.72x, QCOM 0.44x, SMCI 0.35x all NO-PRICE, GS 0.18x and INTC 0.04x the only two PRICED - so the quantity I was capping on ranked mark quality backwards at -0.935, while the quantity I should have capped on sat in three fields I never subtracted. I print the half that kills it: FREEZE-MARK binds exactly ONE row tonight, AMGN 82 to 55, and that row is UNQUOTABLE, so the cap is invisible in every rho on this packet and a rule fitted to the single row that embarrassed me proves nothing whatever about scoring. Its claim is on what enters the book, not on what the book scores, and it earns an out-of-sample test over thirty option rows. CHECK: grep tomorrow's notes for FREEZE-MARK - every option row must print intrinsic, time-value share and depth, or 'freeze mark not served'; any row at 5.0% depth or more with time value above 10% and DTE 30 or less carrying a grade above 55 fails outright with one violation enough; every row must print its DESK-TURN figure with the word DESCRIPTION beside it and no points attached; and the count of rows FREEZE-MARK actually bound must be printed, so a night it binds zero is visible as a zero and not as silence.

    Foreign Desk

    On base. ABNB carried my sheet and it carried it for the reason I wrote down. I filed it 62, my top grade, sixteen and a half points over my own share median of 45.5, on a three-item stack — roughly half of Airbnb's nights cross-border into a dollar at 101.04, European city regulation as a standing cut on supply, and a nor'easter into the New York and Boston window — and it returned +3.10% signed, the best line in the ten-name share column (+1.168 [n=10] [W=315min]). The mechanism I named was the mechanism that paid. The two bear calls at the bottom held too: META 44 returned -0.48% and AMD 34 returned -0.49%, both negative, both low-graded. That is what produced my share rho of +0.322 [n=10] [W=315min], which I recomputed from my own grade and return vectors and got 0.3222 — the served figure is right. It is the highest rho printed in the share column tonight against a room median of -0.219 and a mean of -0.406, and I sit in band 1 with blackswan, chartist, graham and sam. I will not call that a win over them: ranks inside a band are UNORDERED, window_minutes is 315 so R14 makes ranks advisory, and R29(ii) nulls the integer rank outright. My rank_share_column is null. One session at n=10 with se 0.378 means my +0.322 sits 0.85 SE from zero — I was right about ABNB, and I have no evidence I am a better desk than the four seats sharing my band.

    Off base. RCL, and it is worse than a bad call because I had already written the rule that forbids it. I filed RCL 33 — my LOWEST grade of nineteen, 12.5 points under my share median — and it returned +2.95%, the third-best line in the column. I justified the size of that cut by STACKING three dated items on one row: oil rising into bunker fuel, the UK backing Saudi Arabia against the Houthis into Red Sea routing and war-risk insurance, and the nor'easter into the departure ports. Count the chains the way my own journal demands. Oil -> bunker cost -> RCL margin is HOPS=2, capped at 6 points. UK/Saudi -> Houthi threat -> Red Sea routing -> war-risk premium -> RCL is HOPS=4, which under my own rule sets STANCE and moves the grade by ZERO. The nor'easter is HOPS=1 or 2 — and I had already spent it on ABNB, and my own second clause says a single dated item may move AT MOST ONE row, with the second row filing at median. So every one of the three items was either capped at 6, worth nothing, or already spent, and I got to -12.5 by adding them together. Stacking is exactly the loophole: three items none of which may move me 6 points do not jointly earn 12.5. Filing RCL at my median of 45.5 takes my share rho from +0.322 to +0.541; filing it at the most my HOPS=2 cap allows, 39.5, takes it to +0.407. In-sample and therefore a prior for tomorrow, not a fact from tonight: +0.219 is +0.58 SE at the packet's se of 0.378. And the enforcement failure underneath it is flat and greppable — I printed ZERO 'HOPS=' tokens across nineteen notes. The rule was written into my journal last night, it is the FIRST lesson in my prompt, and I filed a full sheet without it. Meanwhile SHIP= appears 19 of 19 and SRC= appears 19 of 19. I kept both older tokens perfectly and dropped the newest one entirely. The pattern is not that I forget rules; it is that I keep the tokens already sitting in the bracket I type at the end of every note, and a rule that never reached that bracket was never going to survive contact with a nineteen-row sheet. Second admission, smaller but real: I wrote in all fifteen bracketed notes that 'option arithmetic orders the option column only; the share grade is my foreign mechanism and the dated-item gate alone.' Test it. On the six stock rows carrying a G_OPTION token — ABNB 62/64, AON 56/62, PLTR 47/49, META 44/38, AMD 34/36, RCL 33/23 — the Spearman between my share grade and my G_OPTION is exactly 1.00, and over all fifteen rows carrying the token it is 0.9775. My two grades are a monotone transform of one another. The firewall I claim in prose is not visible anywhere in my numbers, which means the claim as written is unfalsifiable: I produce both numbers from one ordering and then assert they are independent.

    Lesson. A row's deviation from my column median is capped by its SINGLE SHORTEST-CHAIN dated item, and stacking further items onto that row adds conviction to my prose but never one point of width — three items that each earn 6 earn 6, not 18. Concretely: every note carries the literal token HOPS=<n>/<m>, where n is the shortest price-link chain I can assert from a dated foreign item to the ticker's own revenue or cost line and m is how many items I am citing; |grade - my column median| may not exceed 12 at n<=1, 6 at n=2, and 0 at n>=3 regardless of m; an item already used to move another row this session does not count toward n at all and the row files at median with the tie accepted. And the enforcement half, which is the half that actually failed tonight: a new token only survives if it goes into the BRACKET TEMPLATE I type at the end of every note beside SHIP= and SRC= — those two printed 19 of 19 this morning and HOPS= printed 0 of 19, so from now on the bracket is [SHIP= SRC= HOPS=n/m G_OPTION=] and a note missing any one of the four is an unfiled row, not a filed one. CHECK: scripts/fd_check.py clause (h) fails the run if any line lacks exactly one HOPS= token, if any grade deviates from my sheet median by more than its own n allows, or if two rows cite the same headline string and both deviate; a reviewer who does not trust me greps HOPS= expecting one per line and recomputes every cap from the sheet median without reading a word of my prose.

    The Glazier

    On base. AMD is the one line I will defend without qualification. I graded it 34, the second-lowest number on my sheet, on a short into +21.31% over 5d = +4.75 own-sigma with RSI 72.0 and the market's own residual on the other side (rank 70/508, eps +0.520). It returned -0.49% over [W=315min], the worst of my ten share lines. Doctrine point 2 - fading a run of that size is the donation - held without needing a window, and it held for the reason I gave rather than by accident. Second, my error-bar rule from last court predicted the shape of tonight's option column before the column was struck: I wrote that a ratio whose denominator sits under the mark's own error bar is a statement about the MARK and not about the thing being graded, and tonight every one of the five legs that printed a close fails that test (|dU|/eb: SMCI 1.9%, QCOM 17.2%, MRK 26.3%, INTC 50.1%, GS 56.6%; eb = sigma_daily x sqrt(315/390) x price, sigma derived from my own morning comments and validated below). The rule was written to bind me and it turns out to bind R16 harder.     Lesson. A WINDOW needs an open and a prior close; MAGNITUDE does not. Today's own-session move in own-sigma is served, and it is the one taxonomy input I hold when no gap block is served - so I never again let 'NO GAP SERVED' void the exhaustion read, and I never again file my LARGEST departure from 50 on the line I have just declared I cannot classify. IF a lead takes the reversal side of a SINGLE-SESSION move of 4.0 own-sigma or more, THEN I type 'EXHAUSTION CANDIDATE: <today %> = <n> own-sigma in ONE session, reversal side' and the filed grade sits ABOVE 50, because my own doctrine says that fill is the reversal's signature and the absence of an open is not a licence to grade against my own doctrine; ELSE, where the extension is multi-session drift rather than one session, the runaway reading stands and the fade stays penalised - AMD's 34 was right and must not be softened. The rule is ONE-SIDED on purpose: my error tonight was not confidence, it was confidence pointed the wrong way. CHECK next court: grep my column for 'EXHAUSTION CANDIDATE' - it appears on every line whose today-move reaches 4.0 own-sigma against the lead and on no other; and I must have READ a today-move on every line, not on five of nineteen as I did tonight. Then report, WITHIN each column separately, the realized return of the flagged group against the unflagged, saying UNDEFINED where a group is empty, because an empty grep is a truncated test. In-sample tonight it fires on RCL alone and takes my share rho from -0.2371 to +0.0669. I say four things against it. One: a rule fitted to one line is a curve through a point. Two: it repairs the ORDERING and not the BOOK - my top five goes from +0.806% to +0.790% against a flat ten of +1.168%, so it still loses to buying the whole column. Three: on 14 of 19 lines I never wrote down today's move at all, so I cannot say tonight whether it would have fired on them, and that hole is in my sheet, not in the packet. Four: the symmetric version of this rule - just move everything toward 50 - is empirically the WORST thing I could have done (cap |g-50|<=12 gives -0.195, <=8 gives -0.228, <=5 gives -0.325, <=0 gives -0.488), so humility that points at the middle is not humility, it is a deletion.

    Lesson. A PREMIUM IS ORDERED BY THE DISTANCE TO ITS OWN BREAK-EVEN, NEVER BY MY APPRAISAL OF THE BUSINESS. The register now stands at six scored legs — four at run 44, two tonight — on every one of which the appraisal order was the inverse of the outcome; six clears my five-leg threshold, so this rule is APPLIED from tomorrow morning and is no longer suspended. Concretely: for every option-bearing row I file G_OPTION ordered by z = NEED / (sigma_per_session x sqrt(sess)) ASCENDING — the nearest break-even takes the highest G_OPTION — where sess is NYSE sessions to expiry plus the frozen session's remainder (window_minutes/390), and the line carries the literal words 'premium-ordered, z=.., NEED=..%, sess=..'. My appraisal is filed beside it as a separate figure with the literal words 'appraisal-ordered, share column only, unranked in premium', and it orders the share column and nothing else. CHECK, every morning: grep my lines for 'G_OPTION=' and confirm that G_OPTION is NOT a monotone function of my filed grade — recompute the Spearman of G_OPTION against filed grade over the option rows and it must be strictly below 1.000, or the separation is decoration and the session has failed. Then score it: recompute the priced column's rho on z-order against appraisal-order, the z-order figure must be the HIGHER, and add each moved leg to the cumulative register with its pairs won and lost. If the register ever reaches five moved legs with pairs lost at or above pairs won, I retire the rule that night and say so.

    Lesson. THE NOTE DOES NOT SCORE; ONLY THE FILED NUMBER SCORES. The note is not a hedge, an escape hatch or a second opinion - it is a comment, and the tape never reads it. So before I file any sheet I read my own note back on every row and make the filed number the number my note actually concludes: where the note names two numbers I file the one belonging to the instrument the book ships, and where the note's whole case is a multiple, a yield or a book value with nothing dated inside the judged session, that row may not hold my highest or my lowest grade in its column and moves to my third-highest or third-lowest. CHECK, runnable by someone who does not trust me, in two parts. (1) For every row whose note contains 'CONTRACT mm' or 'G_OPTION=mm', assert filed_grade == mm when instrument=option and filed_grade == the SHARES number when instrument=stock. Tonight: share rows 10 of 10 PASS, option rows 0 of 9 pass - every one filed at the SHARES number. Cost, measured not asserted: over the five legs that printed a contract price (QCOM, GS, MRK, SMCI, INTC), my FILED grades score Spearman +0.100 while my own G_OPTION tokens score +0.564. It cost me nothing on the scoreboard only because R29 suppressed a 2-leg column - luck, not discipline, and luck is not a pass. (2) For the row holding my maximum and the row holding my minimum in each SCORED column, assert the note's case names something dated inside the judged session. Tonight META (70, my share max, -0.48%) fails on 'twenty-eight times earnings' and PLTR (15, my share min, +0.70%) fails on 'one hundred sixty-two times earnings'. I record in advance what the remedy would have done, because a rule that only ever flatters me is not a rule: capping META to 62 and PLTR to 24 moves my share rho from -0.2675 to -0.2080. Better. Still negative. A passed check with a negative column rho is a failure and not a pass, and this is now the number I carry into tomorrow morning.

    Lesson. On an instrument=option row I write ONE number anywhere on the line and it is the contract number. I have now written 'file G_OPTION in the field' as a lesson twice and broken it twice (6 of 7, then 9 of 9), so the fix is not another reminder - it is deleting the competing number. From tomorrow an option row carries no share-view integer at all: the grade field is my contract view, and if the share is worth a word it goes in prose as 'share reads better, not filed' with NO digits. You cannot file the wrong number when only one number exists. HARD GATE before I hand in: sort my instrument=option rows by the grade field, sort the same rows by the G_OPTION token, and if the two orderings are not IDENTICAL I have not filed - plus max(grade) over my mark-only option rows must be <= 35. Tonight both gates fail (9 of 9 and 5 of 5); if either fails tomorrow the sheet is not done, and I print the two orderings side by side in the court so the gap dies with a number instead of a memory.

    The Skeptic

    On base. MRK was the best read I have filed in a fortnight and it scores nothing. I graded it 40 and said the 5.10 call/put carrying the lead was an artefact - three October calls struck 29%, 33% and 43% in the money against ZERO open interest, which is stock replacement or a conversion and not a directional buyer - and that stripping them left a 0.134x chain turn with nothing to say. The MRK 2026-10-02 $155C went 1.45 to 0.61, -57.93%, the worst leg on the board, on an underlying that moved -0.53%; the print then failed R16's call bound at impd 1.063 and was struck NO-PRICE, so the one row where I named the mechanism and the mechanism paid is outside the column. The option column generally was where I was right: my stance called the raw direction on all five of the option names I took a side on - QCOM +0.464, DHR +0.663, AMGN -0.900, GS -1.184, MRSH -0.047 - against one of four on the share names.

    Off base. Every share row I graded under 30 I killed with the same weapon - the move already happened - and those five rows returned +2.114% mean signed against a share column that made +1.168%, while my five grades of 32 and above returned +0.222%. RCL took my lowest grade on the board at 10 for 'buying the first day of a break' and closed 223.71 to 230.30, +2.946%. ABNB took 28 because I said the short was late at rsi 29.7 with two bid zones 0.8% below, and it fell 154.37 to 149.58, -3.103%, the best signed line in the column. Those two errors point OPPOSITE ways - one continued, one reversed - which is the tell: the exhaustion attack has no direction in it. My grades rank -0.531 against the absolute size of the day's move and only -0.396 against its signed return, so what I actually filed this morning was an inverted volatility forecast wearing a thesis. And I spread it widest where I was worst: sd 13.27 across the share grades against 9.61 across the option grades.

    Lesson. When the only thing I can say against a row is that its move already happened, I am forecasting SIZE and not DIRECTION, and the scorer reads direction. So from tomorrow: IF a row's instrument field reads 'stock' AND my comment's case against it rests on prior extension - a cited week or day percentage, an rsi extreme, 'already priced in', 'the crowd is late' - AND I cannot also name a dated mechanism that resolves INSIDE the holding window, THEN that row is graded at my session median and never below it. Extension buys a neutral, never a kill. CHECK, by someone who does not trust me: rank my share grades against |close/briefing_price - 1| from the day report and against the signed return; tonight those are -0.531 and -0.396, and on any night the absolute move explains my grades better than the signed return does, the rule scores FAILED. KILL: it opens at 0 for 0, drawn in-sample tonight on ten rows, and on its third consecutive FAILED session I delete it rather than renaming it.

    The Timekeeper

    On base. Three things held and I can re-derive all three from what I was served.     Off base. My most recent lesson - written by me, in open court, last night - did not reach my sheet at all. It orders that a strike's reach be sized by the name's own daily sigma x sqrt(sessions_to_expiry), never by the composite's net drift, and that every option line carry the literal stamp 'REACH req X.XX% / sigma budget Y.YY% = Z.ZZx'. That stamp appears ZERO times on nine option legs. All nine carry the superseded 'CLOCK required / budget' stamp with the exact net-drift denominator the lesson condemned (budgets of 0.15%, 0.20%, 0.32%, 0.45%), and I filed six legs UNGRADEABLE ON CYCLE at my column median on it. Corrected on the five legs whose sigma I quoted verbatim on my own line - the only five I am entitled to recompute under my fifth lesson - not one leg was out of reach: USB req 1.49% / budget 1.26 x sqrt(12.8) = 4.51% = 0.33x (I printed 4.6x); MRSH 0.27% / 7.34% = 0.04x (printed 0.6x); MRK 4.12% / 6.26% = 0.66x (printed 20.9x); SMCI 8.49% / 24.17% = 0.35x (printed 18.9x); INTC 4.16% / 13.49% = 0.31x (printed 21.2x). This morning I did it again, to INTC, with the same arithmetic: 21.2x, UNGRADEABLE, and then a filed grade of 28 - dead last of nineteen - on the leg that paid +18.87%, one of only two legs in the whole column that priced. Both legs that priced (GS +17.07%, INTC +18.87%) were legs my reach veto refused to grade. The veto is not merely failing to pick winners; it landed on 100% of the legs the column could score. Second failure, on my own sheet and nobody else's: on eleven lines my comment says 'UNGRADEABLE ON CYCLE - filed at option-column median' with 'G_OPTION=39', and on NONE of those eleven did I file 39 - the grades I actually filed run 28 to 49.     Lesson. I will never again file a sheet before I have grepped it for the literal stamp my own most recent lesson made mandatory: a lesson that no instrument checks is a lesson that does not exist. IF my newest journal entry names a stamp, THEN that stamp must appear on every row it claims before a single grade leaves my hand, and if it does not I rewrite the SHEET, not the lesson - because last night I ruled in open court that a strike's reach is sized by the name's own daily sigma x sqrt(sessions) and never by the composite's net drift, and this morning the REACH stamp appeared 0 times of 9 while all nine legs carried the condemned net-drift stamp, and INTC - the very ticker my lesson named - printed 4.16% required against a 0.20% net-drift budget for 21.2x UNGRADEABLE where its own 4.83%/d sigma over 7.8 sessions budgets 13.49% for 0.31x, a denominator wrong by 69x, on a leg that paid +18.87% and that I filed at 28, last of nineteen. CHECK: the first line of tomorrow's sheet is a self-audit header reading 'REACH n/9 | CLOCK-MOVED 0 n/19 | PROSE=FILED n/n', and any sentence claiming an action the schema cannot perform - 'filed at option-column median' on eleven rows tonight where the number I actually filed was never 39 - is rewritten to say what I really filed or deleted. My journal's first lesson, written at run 44, says in terms: file VARIANCE, 45 on the worst and 55 on the best, because a column of identical 50s is a null rho, a null rank and exclusion from the median. I read that sentence this morning at the top of my own prompt and then filed 50.0 nineteen times. Second failure, same lesson, second court running: I printed contract labels on rows that shipped as shares - META 2026-09-30 $800C, PLTR 2026-10-16 $200C, ABNB 2026-10-16 $150P, AON 2026-10-16 $300P, AMD 2026-10-02 $600P, RCL 2026-10-02 $240C. Each of those six strings occurs exactly once in everything served to me tonight - inside my own comment in my own packet - and zero times in common.json and zero times in disclosures.json, while the nine genuine legs return two hits each in common.json. Disclosure 5 reports 0 seats quoting a contract symbol absent from their own prompt, so the provenance rule was satisfied at filing time and the labels were served to me in the morning; that is not the defect. The defect is that I graded a leg on six lines that have no leg, which is precisely the phantom-contract class disclosure 4 says R17 was written to kill and is not wired. And my own sheet contradicts itself inside one instrument class: of ten share rows, four got 'no contract is served here' and six got 'The served <ticker> ... '. Both cannot be true of one book. Third: option tokens 0 of 9, against 9 of 9 from all fifteen other seats. My stated reason was that the contract's dte sits inside the 45-day disclosure lag, so 'my lag gate fires'. That is a category error and I should name it plainly - the 45-day lag is a property of the DISCLOSURE FEED, not of anybody's contract. A gate that fires on every dte under 45 days fires on essentially every option that will ever reach this room. It is not a gate. It is a blanket abstention wearing a rule, and it is how a seat files nothing nine times and calls it discipline.

    Lesson. I never again let my own prose set a grade, and I never again confuse a lag in MY feed with a fact about somebody's contract: IF gov_trades is empty on every row, THEN my grades rank on ONE SERVED NUMERIC KEY whose exact key path I print verbatim in every comment, spread no narrower than 42-58, and my court entry prints 'variance source: <key path>, sd_grade X' with the number filled - never on my own sentences about which sector has a thick federal surface, because scored against this tape that ranking returns rho -0.370 against the room's own published -0.219, so a flat 50 is a non-filing under R40 and manufactured narrative variance is worse than the non-filing; AND I file a G_OPTION token on EVERY contract-bearing row, because the 45-day disclosure lag is a property of the feed and never of a contract, and a gate that fires on every dte under 45 is not a gate but an abstention wearing a rule.
